chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The man and the woman shall not be stoned until four witnesses testify against both of them to the sexual intercourse, the penetration, and the entering — like the applicator in the kohl container.'

key_terms.الْإِدْخَالُ: idkhal — entering/insertion, used here to specify the exact act required for the hadd to apply
key_terms.الْإِيلَاجُ: ilaj — penetration, the technical legal term for the moment of sexual entry
key_terms.الْجِمَاعُ: jima' — sexual intercourse, the act of copulation
key_terms.الْمِيلُ فِي الْمُكْحُلَةِ: mil fi al-mukhhula — needle in the kohl container, a classical legal simile for full penetration
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: rajm — stoning, the prescribed punishment (hadd) for proven adultery under Islamic law

ai.seo_question: How many witnesses are required for stoning in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm) for adultery (zina) requires four eyewitnesses who specifically attest to the act of sexual penetration, described with the vivid legal simile of a needle entering a kohl container. This extremely high evidentiary threshold — four witnesses to the actual act of penetration — effectively makes the formal imposition of this punishment nearly impossible in practice, which classical Shia jurists understood as a deliberate feature of the law. The ruling reflects the Imam's legal teaching in the context of fiqh al-hudud (the law of prescribed penalties).
